findings.message: Review round 4 fixed one case: the card-mismatch refusal in the correct/delete services now throws a ToolError, so `userFacing` lets the REST API answer 400 and the bulk card shows the text. Other refusals added in this change still throw a plain `Error`, so `userFacing` is false. REST then answers 500 `internal` with only a reference, and the guidance text is lost. Affected: `guardFixable` (week submitted, or approved and locked), `guardLock`/`lockRefusal` (guards.ts:31), `guardDayTotal` ('more than 24 h', guards.ts:41), `writeCorrection` ('no project X', correct.ts:37), `requestChange` (week is draft; an open request already exists; request.ts:34-37), `decideRequest` (request already decided; entry changed since; decide-request.ts:24-26,65), and `writeReopen` (reopen.ts:11). Fix: throw these as `ToolError(..., "invalid_input")`, like `refuse()` and `decide()`/`writeRemind` already do. Extend the round-4 `userFacing` test to these refusals.
findings.scenario: REST call to correct_time_entry for an entry on a submitted week → HTTP 500 {error:'internal', ref} instead of 400 with 'is submitted and waiting for approval… use request_time_change'. Same for decide_change_request apply after the entry's revision moved → 500 instead of 400 'the entry changed since the request'.

findings.message: The 070 mock section still draws a per-row '✦ Fix these hours' button and says 'An approved week has no "Fix these hours" button'. Amendment 4, the README and the e2e test all say rows carry pins and no per-row Fix buttons, so code and mock disagree. The block also has the wrong heading comment ('068 Overview deltas' above the 073 section), and the diff adds sections owned by other changes (066, 068, 069, 071, 072, 073), which looks like a carried-over merge. Fix: update the 070 section to show the pin and chat-suggestion flow, and drop or justify the sections other changes own.

A `when` check that throws counts as 'not applicable', so its suggestion silently disappears. `pageContext` (apps/web/app/actions/chat.ts:41) also returns null for every failure, including `SignedInElsewhere`, so the header falls back to the generic text. Suggestions are only an aid, but a check that couldn't run should be logged at least, not treated as false.
findings.scenario: teamWeek throws (DB blip) → 'Approve submitted timesheets' isn't offered and nothing is logged.

findings.message: `earlierSession` returns null as soon as the first cookie name it finds fails to decode. It never tries the other name (`__Secure-` vs plain). A browser holding a stale `__Secure-` cookie next to a valid plain one keeps its earlier session alive after a switch. Fix: on a decode failure, continue to the next name.
findings.scenario: Browser has a stale __Secure-authjs.session-token and a live authjs.session-token, then signs in as someone else → the live earlier session is not revoked.

findings.message: This change adds jsonb columns that code reads for logic to retention `fields`: `delivery.proposal.meta`, `it_access.change.detail` and `career.history.detail`. When a row is anonymised, `applyRule` replaces a jsonb value with `'{}'` (packages/core/src/privacy/apply.ts:15). `delivery.proposal.meta` holds the `withdrawn` flag that `ACTIVE` filters on (queries.ts:59), plus the sha, pr and verdict that the sync fingerprints. `it_access.change.detail` holds `products`, `skuIds` and `externalUserId`, which the queued-change runner dereferences (apply.ts:26 `c.detail.products.join`). Fix: anonymise only the personal keys inside these documents, or move the personal text into its own column that retention can null. If the structure has no person in it, list the column under `keep` with the reason.
findings.scenario: An erasure request for the Admin who approved an it_access change that is still queued sets `detail` to {}. The next apply run throws a TypeError on `c.detail.products`, so the whole due batch fails. Separately, a proposal that was withdrawn and then idle for a year gets anonymised: `meta.withdrawn` is lost, and the proposal shows up again in the active lists.

findings.message: Change requests are closed in only one case: `submitWeek` completes requests in status 'reopened'. If the week is reopened by an Admin's `reopen_week`, or sent back by `reject_week`, its pending and needs_info requests stay open. The owner then fixes the entry directly, which bumps its revision. The request still sits on Team time and in the 'Review change requests' suggestion, and `apply` refuses it as stale. The approver can only decline it, and the owner's 'Change requested' notice stays up. Fix: when a week leaves submitted or approved through any path, close or cancel its open requests in the same transaction and emit `changeDecided`/`changeCompleted`. Add a test over reopen_week, reject_week and a decide-reopen.
findings.scenario: Kasun asks to change an entry on his approved 2026-W42 (pending). Sahan reopens the week with reopen_week, Kasun corrects the entry and resubmits. The request is still 'pending' on Team time, and decide_change_request apply returns 'the entry changed since the request'.
